prompt: Three radio buttons in a ButtonGroup pick a theme. Complete getSelectedTheme (the chosen button's action command, or "none") and refresh so a label always reads like "Theme: dark".
explanation: A ButtonGroup enforces that at most one of its buttons is selected, and group.getSelection() hands back the selected ButtonModel -- or null before the user picks anything, which is the case you must guard. Reading getActionCommand() off that model keeps your code independent of the label text shown on screen, so renaming a button cannot break the logic. Registering the same refresh call on every button means one method keeps the display in step with the group.
hints: group.getSelection() returns a ButtonModel, and it is null until something is selected.
ButtonModel has getActionCommand(), which is the string that was passed to setActionCommand.
refresh can simply call your own getSelectedTheme() and concatenate it after "Theme: ".
